notes: JetLagged, the custom Canvas / custom layout sample. :app declares 9 @Preview functions, all catalogued; MultiDevicePreview is declared in the same module. Carries one patch, patches/0001-default-extra-colors-to-light-palette.patch: LocalExtraColors' default is an empty JetLaggedExtraColors(), and HeartRateGraph throws IllegalArgumentException (waveLineColors requires 2+ colors) when it reads it outside JetLaggedTheme. HeartRateCard and JetLaggedScreen are @Preview-annotated in place and install no theme, so without the patch HeartRateCard and all four JetLaggedScreen device previews fail standalone, in Android Studio as well. The patch defaults the local to the light palette, one line, and is the change to offer upstream; no preview is excluded, and all 16 renders succeed with it. JetLaggedScreen itself renders but is NOT catalogued: its windowSizeClass parameter is a value class (WindowWidthSizeClass), so Kotlin mangles the JVM method to JetLaggedScreen-uVTuf4s, discovery reports that mangled name as the function name, and the spec join (which matches the source name the pre-flight requires) never pairs it — a toolchain gap in compose-ai-tools discovery / the export driver, not something this import should paper over. 8 of the 9 functions are catalogued; the hero is the heart-rate card the patch makes renderable. Built from UNMODIFIED upstream android/compose-samples (main), replacing the catalog preview.coo.ee served from the yschimke/compose-samples fork: that fork's `previews` branch carried roughly ten thousand lines of catalog-only preview sources that no longer apply to upstream, and none of them is carried over — this import renders upstream's own @Preview functions only, and every spec entry names one. The Theme control comes from the sample's own theme composable via `themes` in the spec, replacing the fork's re-themed Material 3 tab. Each sample is its own Gradle build in a subdirectory of the repository, hence workingDirectory. Licence: Apache-2.0.
